items.example: We need plates, cups and whatnot for the party.
items.exampleTr: Parti için tabak, bardak falan filan lazım.
items.simple: And other things like that. You don't need to name them all.
dialogue: A: What do you need from the shop?
B: Just bread, milk and whatnot.
items.note: Listenin sonunda; 'and stuff' un biraz daha renkli hali.

items.tr: aşağı yukarı, üç aşağı beş yukarı
items.example: It's about two hours from here, give or take.
items.exampleTr: Buradan aşağı yukarı iki saat.
items.simple: About this much, maybe a little more or a little less.
dialogue: A: How many people are coming?
B: Thirty, give or take.
items.note: Sayıdan sonra ya da önce: 'give or take ten minutes'.

items.tr: ya da ona benzer bir şey
items.example: He said he was 'reassessing his priorities', or something along those lines.
items.exampleTr: 'Önceliklerini yeniden değerlendirdiğini' ya da ona benzer bir şey söyledi.
items.simple: You don't remember the exact words, but it was like that.
dialogue: A: What exactly did the email say?
B: 'Please see me urgently', or something along those lines.
items.note: Birinin sözünü kabaca aktarırken.

items.example: I like hiking, camping, that sort of thing.
items.exampleTr: Doğa yürüyüşü, kamp, o tarz şeyleri severim.
items.simple: Things like the ones you just said.
dialogue: A: What do you do at the weekend?
B: Gardening, cooking, that sort of thing.
items.note: ABD'de daha çok 'that kind of thing'.

items.example: There'll be speeches, cake, balloons and all that jazz.
items.exampleTr: Konuşmalar, pasta, balonlar falan feşmekan olacak.
items.simple: And all the other usual things that go with it.
dialogue: A: Is it a proper wedding?
B: Oh yes, church, white dress and all that jazz.
items.note: Esprili, biraz alaycı; sıkıcı/şatafatlı şeyler için.

items.example: I saw what's-his-name from your old job at the gym.
items.exampleTr: Gym'de senin eski işten şeyi gördüm, adı neydi.
items.simple: A word you use when you forget a man's name.
dialogue: A: Who was that at the door?
B: What's-his-name, the guy from number six.
items.note: Kadın için 'what's-her-name'; çok gündelik.

items.example: Pass me that thingamajig for opening tins.
items.exampleTr: Konserve açmaya yarayan şu zımbırtıyı uzatsana.
items.simple: A silly word for a thing when you forget what it's called.
dialogue: A: What are you looking for?
B: The little thingamajig that charges my headphones.
items.note: Esprili; 'thingy', 'whatsit' de aynı anlamda.

items.example: I'll be there at seven or thereabouts.
items.exampleTr: Yedi ya da civarında orada olurum.
items.simple: Near that number, time or place, but not exact.
dialogue: A: How old is the house?
B: A hundred years or thereabouts.
items.note: Saat, yaş, fiyattan sonra.

items.example: We can fit six in the car at a push.
items.exampleTr: Zorlarsak arabaya altı kişi sığabiliriz.
items.simple: It's possible, but only if you really try hard.
dialogue: A: Can you finish it by Thursday?
B: At a push, yes. Friday would be safer.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi; ABD'de 'if push comes to shove'.

items.example: He's the black sheep of the family, as it were.
items.exampleTr: O, tabiri caizse, ailenin yüz karası.
items.simple: You say this after using words in a funny or not quite exact way.
dialogue: A: So you're back on the market?
B: Back on the dating scene, as it were.
items.note: Hafif esprili ve kibar; ironiyle de kullanılır.

items.example: We're married, in a manner of speaking. We just never had a wedding.
items.exampleTr: Bir bakıma evliyiz. Sadece hiç düğün yapmadık.
items.simple: It's true in one way, but not exactly true.
dialogue: A: So are you the boss now?
B: In a manner of speaking. Nobody else wanted the job.
items.note: 'Sort of' un daha kibar/esprili hali.

items.tr: bana kalırsa, ne bileyim, belki de
items.example: For all I know, he could be in Australia by now.
items.exampleTr: Ne bileyim, şimdiye Avustralya'da bile olabilir.
items.simple: I really don't know, so anything could be true.
dialogue: A: Where's your brother these days?
B: For all I know, he's still in Berlin.
items.note: Bilgisizliği vurgular; hafif umursamazlık.

items.en: if you know what I mean
items.tr: anladın sen onu, ne demek istediğimi anladın
items.example: He's a bit... intense, if you know what I mean.
items.exampleTr: Biraz... yoğun biri, anladın sen onu.
items.simple: You hope the other person understands the thing you don't say.
dialogue: A: How's your new flatmate?
B: He's very... clean, if you know what I mean.
items.note: İma ederken; bazen sadece dolgu kelime.

items.en: off the top of my head
items.tr: aklıma ilk gelen, hemen şimdi aklımdan
items.example: Off the top of my head, I'd say about fifty quid.
items.exampleTr: Şöyle bir aklımdan, elli pound civarı derim.
items.simple: Said fast, without checking or thinking for long.
dialogue: A: What's the wifi password?
B: I don't know it off the top of my head.
items.note: 'I can't remember off the top of my head' = şu an çıkaramadım.

items.example: Let's just say they're more than friends, if you catch my drift.
items.exampleTr: Arkadaştan öte diyelim, ne demek istediğimi anladıysan.
items.simple: You hope the other person understands what you are hinting at.
dialogue: A: Is the new manager strict?
B: Let's say he likes things done his way, if you catch my drift.
items.note: Gayriresmî; ima için. 'if you know what I mean' ile yakın ama daha imalı.

items.en: the long and the short of it
items.example: The long and the short of it is, we're moving to Leeds.
items.exampleTr: Uzun lafın kısası, Leeds'e taşınıyoruz.
items.simple: The main point, without all the details.
dialogue: A: So what happened with the car?
B: The long and the short of it is, it's dead.
items.note: Uzun bir hikâyeyi özetlemeden önce.

items.example: Sorry, my phone rang. Now, where was I?
items.exampleTr: Pardon, telefonum çaldı. Eee, nerede kalmıştım?
items.simple: You say this when you were talking and forgot your place.
dialogue: A: Sorry, carry on with the story.
B: Right, where was I? Oh yes, the police turned up.
items.note: Sözün bölününce; 'Anyway, where was I?' çok tipik.

items.example: You can bring snacks, drinks or what have you.
items.exampleTr: Atıştırmalık, içecek ya da her neyse getirebilirsin.
items.simple: Or other similar things.
dialogue: A: What should I put in the box?
B: Old clothes, books or what have you.
items.note: Biraz eski usul ama yaygın; 'and whatnot' gibi.

items.example: I just need to pick up a few bits and bobs from the shop.
items.exampleTr: Dükkândan birkaç ufak tefek şey almam lazım.
items.simple: Lots of small different things.
dialogue: A: What's in that drawer?
B: Oh, just bits and bobs. Batteries, string, keys.
items.note: İngiliz İngilizcesi, gayriresmî; ABD'de 'odds and ends'.

items.en: and so on and so forth
items.example: He went on about his diet, his gym, his protein shakes and so on and so forth.
items.exampleTr: Diyetini, spor salonunu, protein içeceklerini ve saire ve saire anlattı durdu.
items.simple: And more and more of the same things.
dialogue: A: What did the trainer talk about?
B: Teamwork, synergy, and so on and so forth.
items.note: Sıkılmışlık ya da alay tonu katar.

items.example: We had a band, fireworks, the whole shebang.
items.exampleTr: Orkestra, havai fişek, her şey vardı.
items.simple: Everything, all of it, with nothing left out.
dialogue: A: Did you just buy a new bike?
B: Bike, helmet, lights, the whole shebang.
items.note: Gayriresmî, esprili; 'the whole lot' ile yakın.

items.example: I'll be ready at sevenish. Well, seven-thirty-ish.
items.exampleTr: Yedi gibi hazır olurum. Yani yedi buçuk gibi.
items.simple: A little bit, more or less, not exactly.
dialogue: A: Are you ready to go?
B: Ish. Give me five minutes.
items.note: Tek başına cevap da olur: 'Are you ready?' 'Ish.'

items.example: How can I put this... your cooking is very brave.
items.exampleTr: Nasıl desem... yemeklerin çok cesur.
items.simple: You say this when you need time to find kind words for bad news.
dialogue: A: Did you like my poem?
B: Well, how can I put this... it's very long.
items.note: Kırıcı bir şeyi yumuşatmadan hemen önce.

items.example: I want a job that matters, if that makes sense.
items.exampleTr: Bir anlamı olan bir iş istiyorum, anlatabildim mi.
items.simple: You check that the other person understood what you tried to say.
dialogue: A: Why do you want to move?
B: I just need a change, if that makes sense.
items.note: Çok yaygın, özellikle genç konuşmacılarda; bazen dolgu.

items.example: Not gonna lie, I cried at the end of that film.
items.exampleTr: Yalan yok, o filmin sonunda ağladım.
items.simple: Words you say before you admit something honestly.
dialogue: A: How was the new burger place?
B: Not gonna lie, it was amazing.
items.note: Çok gayriresmî; mesajda 'ngl' diye yazılır.

items.example: Shoes off at the door, you know the drill.
items.exampleTr: Ayakkabılar kapıda çıkarılıyor, usulü biliyorsun.
items.simple: You already know how this works, so I don't need to explain.
dialogue: A: What do I do with my bag?
B: Same as always, you know the drill.
items.note: Tekrarlanan rutinler için, gayriresmî.
